lines.text: as he is in his urge to assert his authority and in his pathetic
selt-deception; and it brings him back to his true self—as he
receives himself from God's hand: as the justified man, who
in his spiritual freedom does not need to lower his eyes
before any man since he has lowered them before God.
For such a man the world too, and human society, is trans-
figured. Instead of an unscrupulous desire to press one's
claims at all costs, we have the spirit of sincere, honest and
self-forgetful service. Instead of envious ill-will, and ruth-
lessness, we have a cheerful spirit of mutual regard and
esteem. Instead of reserve and tense self-concern, we have
friendliness, frankness and joy in fellowship with others. If
our parable persuades anyone to adopt this new way of life,
on such a one Jesus has exercised His liberating redemptive
